title: Barda Hills Wildlife Sanctuary Porbandar - Explore Gujarat’s Hidden Nature Gem
content:
Barda Hills Wildlife Sanctuary, Porbandar

 Nestled near the coastal city of Porbandar, the Barda Hills Wildlife Sanctuary is one of Gujarat’s most captivating natural reserves. Spread over lush hills and rugged terrain, this sanctuary offers a perfect escape for nature lovers, wildlife enthusiasts, and photographers. Known locally as Jam Barda, it was once a private hunting ground for the royal families of Jamnagar and Porbandar, and today it stands as a thriving ecosystem rich in flora and fauna.

Wildlife and Nature:

The Barda Hills Sanctuary covers an area of around 192 square kilometers and is home to a diverse range of wildlife. It shelters species like leopards, wolves, sambar deer, chinkara, hyenas, and blue bulls (nilgai). The sanctuary is also a paradise for bird watchers, with numerous resident and migratory birds such as eagles, owls, crested serpent eagles, and partridges found here.

The dense forests of babool, acacia, and euphorbia create a perfect habitat for these animals and offer stunning scenic views. The sanctuary’s hilly landscape, natural springs, and peaceful environment make it an ideal destination for eco-tourism and nature exploration.

History and Significance:

The Barda Hills area once served as the royal hunting reserve of the Maharajas of Jamnagar and Porbandar. Today, it stands protected under Gujarat’s Forest Department, promoting wildlife conservation and environmental awareness. It’s also an important watershed that supports the local villages through natural springs and streams.

How to Reach Barda Hills Wildlife Sanctuary:

  • By Air: The nearest airport is Porbandar Airport (around 15 km away).
  • By Train: Porbandar Railway Station is the closest railhead, located about 15-20 km from the sanctuary.
  • By Road: Barda Hills can be reached by road from Porbandar (15 km), Jamnagar (100 km), or Rajkot (170 km) via private taxis or GSRTC buses.

Visiting Time and Entry Fee:

  • Timings: 7:00 AM to 6:00 PM (Closed during monsoon - June to September).
  • Entry Fee: ₹20 per person (approx.) and extra charges for vehicles and cameras.
  • Best Time to Visit: October to February, when the weather is cool and ideal for exploring wildlife.

Things to Do:

  • Wildlife spotting and bird watching
  • Trekking through scenic trails
  • Nature photography and picnicking
  • Exploring nearby villages and local culture
